title: Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night
content:
Do not go gentle into that good night,
Old age should burn and rave at close of day;
Rage, rage against the dying of the light.

Though wise men at their end know dark is right,
Because their words had forked no lightning they
Do not go gentle into that good night.

title: The Road Not Taken
content:
Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;

I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

title: Ozymandias
content:
I met a traveller from an antique land,
Who said—'Two vast and trunkless legs of stone
Stand in the desert. . . . Near them, on the sand,
Half sunk a shattered visage lies, whose frown,
And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command,
Tell that its sculptor well those passions read.'
'My name is Ozymandias, King of Kings;
Look on my Works, ye Mighty, and despair!'

title: The Raven (Opening)
content:
Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary,
Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore—
While I nodded, nearly napping, suddenly there came a tapping,
As of some one gently rapping, rapping at my chamber door.
'’Tis some visitor,' I muttered, 'tapping at my chamber door—
Only this and nothing more.'

title: Sonnet 18
content:
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer's lease hath all too short a date;
Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines,
And often is his gold complexion dimm'd;
So long as men can breathe or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.

title: Hope is the thing with feathers
content:
'Hope' is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard -
And sore must be the storm -
That could abash the little Bird
That kept so many warm -

title: Still I Rise
content:
You may write me down in history
With your bitter, twisted lies,
You may trod me in the very dirt
But still, like dust, I'll rise.

Does my sassiness upset you?
Why are you beset with gloom?
’Cause I walk like I've got oil wells
Pumping in my living room.

title: Fire and Ice
content:
Some say the world will end in fire,
Some say in ice.
From what I’ve tasted of desire
I hold with those who favor fire.
But if it had to perish twice,
I think I know enough of hate
To say that for destruction ice
Is also great
And would suffice.

title: Jabberwocky
content:
’Twas brillig, and the slithy toves
Did gyre and gimble in the wabe:
All mimsy were the borogoves,
And the mome raths outgrabe.

'Beware the Jabberwock, my son!
The jaws that bite, the claws that catch!
Beware the Jubjub bird, and shun
The frumious Bandersnatch!'

title: She Walks in Beauty
Invictus
content:
Out of the night that covers me,
Black as the pit from pole to pole,
I thank whatever gods may be
For my unconquerable soul.

In the fell clutch of circumstance
I have not winced nor cried aloud.
Under the bludgeonings of chance
My head is bloody, but unbowed.

I am the master of my fate,
I am the captain of my soul.

title: We Real Cool
content:
THE POOL PLAYERS.
SEVEN AT THE GOLDEN SHOVEL.

We real cool. We
Left school. We

Lurk late. We
Strike straight. We

Sing sin. We
Thin gin. We

Jazz June. We
Die soon.

title: XIV. Retreat of Prospero (A Solo)
content:
Today I signed the final devolution of authority to the Network. They called it an 'optimization of global friction.'
They brought their pressed sand to show me how they could manage better than a crown, a constitution, or even a conscience.
They smiled with the clean, unblinking eyes of men who have never smelled the mud of a trench, the rust of a barred gate, or felt the tears wash upon their face from the shame and weight of duty.
They believe they are building a palace of pure logic. Yet with their eyes like jewels, they cannot see they are building a cage.
A philosopher cannot govern a world that no longer believes in substance.
When the people look at the sky, they no longer see the sky and all its glory; they see data packets.
When they look at the mountain, they do not feel its ancient weight; they calculate its yield.
I leave them a perfect, frictionless void.
Let us see how long they can stand before the cold wind knocks, and finds nobody home.
Farewell, The Curator

title: XVII. Chorale in G: Vain Presage
content:
Glad was O’man when the River loosed his soles from stone; the farther bank kept no country, only Garden, Bone, Ember.
was 6 the number? The Mountain: rings; iron answers passed beneath the Water and fell away as Bell, Dust, Ground.
I heard 'very heavy attack' carried lightly between clean hands; Black Fire spread o’er the current, leaving Drowned, Flame, Blood.
when 'not too long' became the measure, real rain fell without Mercy; taking Form, Ash, Dead.
Now the corpse of the thing walked the Mountain’s halls; the Homunculus had found a body among Form, Absence, Dust.
for Quality was scarce here too; The Eye blinked once, and Glass drew Breath enough to become Glass, Breath, Evidence.
a fish crossed below without Presage; no god troubled its current; above, a Bird, Dove, Garden.
better Beauty Escaped, Dignified; no Curator framed it, no crown possessed it; Form, Arrest, Dignity.
wage unknown. The Mountain ceased ringing; Water carried no promise to either shore. Only Cinder, Elegy, Ash.
